about: The figures in Dinis Cruz's white paper "Dynamic Weather-Driven Algarve Tourism Campaign", each checked against a primary source where one was found. Status is one of: confirmed by primary source, differs from primary source, source unconfirmed. Distances are computed great-circle (haversine, Earth radius 6371.0088 km) from OpenStreetMap coordinates; they are straight lines, and road distances are longer. Kept by analyst.london-billboard@AgentiCCells.dinis; details in team/rounds/1/data/FIGURES.md.

figures.claim: The Algarve has over 300 days of sunshine a year
figures.white_paper_wording: the Algarve's 300+ days of sunshine; over 300 days of sunshine a year

primary.value: Faro airport: on average 9.0 days a year with no sunshine at all and 37.2 days with 20% or less of the possible sunshine, so about 356 days with some sunshine and about 328 with more than 20%; 3044.4 hours of sunshine a year
primary.publisher: IPMA (then Instituto de Meteorologia), Normal Climatológica Faro/Aeroporto (554)

figures.note: True if a day of sunshine means a day with some sun. Faro station only, not the whole Algarve. IPMA's 1991-2020 normal for Faro has no sunshine figures. The paper's own source is a tour operator's page, not primary.

figures.claim: The Algarve has dozens of Blue Flag beaches
figures.white_paper_wording: dozens of Blue Flag beaches (its source list says 87 Blue Flag beaches)

primary.value: Algarve: 94 Blue Flag sites, of which 86 are beaches (the other 8 are 6 marinas and 2 boats, our count from the list)
primary.publisher: ABAAE, Associação Bandeira Azul de Ambiente e Educação (Blue Flag in Portugal)

figures.note: "Dozens" holds. The paper's 87 is from an earlier year; in 2026 it is 86 beaches. Albufeira alone has 24 beaches and its marina.

figures.claim: January days in the Algarve average around five hours of sunshine
figures.white_paper_wording: January days in the Algarve still average around five hours of sunshine

primary.value: 182.1 hours of sunshine in January at Faro airport, about 5.9 hours a day
primary.publisher: IPMA (then Instituto de Meteorologia), Normal Climatológica Faro/Aeroporto (554)

figures.note: Nearer six hours than five (182.1 / 31 = 5.87). Say "about six hours a day in January at Faro (IPMA, 1971-2000)".

figures.claim: London often sees only about one hour of sunshine a day in January
figures.white_paper_wording: while London often sees only about one hour

primary.value: 59.0 hours of sunshine in January at Heathrow, about 1.9 hours a day (our mean of the 30 monthly totals; 1971-2000 gives 55.1 hours, 1.8 a day)
primary.publisher: Met Office, historic station data, Heathrow (London Airport)

figures.note: About two hours a day, not one. The Met Office's own averages table (https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/research/climate/maps-and-data/uk-climate-averages/gcpsveqyg) loads by script and was not read; our mean may differ from it by a little. Together with Faro: about three times London's January sunshine, not five.

figures.claim: Example temperatures of 24 to 26 C in the Algarve against 9 to 14 C in London
figures.white_paper_wording: "Algarve today: 24°C & sunny. London: 9°C & drizzle."; "Next 3 days in Algarve: 26°C sun / 25°C sun / 24°C sun"

primary.value: Faro airport mean daily maximum: November 19.6 C, December 17.1 C, January 16.3 C; days of 25 C or more: November 0.3, December 0.0, January 0.0

figures.note: The paper's numbers are examples, not claims, but 24 to 26 C is a summer or late-spring value at Faro, rare from November to February. Heathrow's January mean maximum is 8.4 C (our mean of Met Office monthly data, 1991-2020), so the London side of the example is fair.

figures.claim: Roughly 50% of Algarve hotels close for the winter months
figures.white_paper_wording: in typical years roughly 50% of Algarve hotels close for the winter months (due to lack of visitors)
figures.note: The paper gives no source. INE publishes each month the share of tourist accommodation establishments closed or without guests, but no Algarve figure for a winter month in a normal year was found from INE itself in this round. Do not use the 50% until one is.

figures.claim: The flight from London to Faro takes about 2h40m
figures.note: No primary timetable was checked (airline timetables were not used, so as to name no airline). Computed great-circle distance: Gatwick to Faro 1688 km (911 nm), Heathrow to Faro 1713 km, Luton 1757 km, Stansted 1774 km. Any flight time on the screen stays an invented example.

figures.claim: You could be in the Algarve in about five hours
figures.white_paper_wording: You could be here in 5 hours; Only 5 hours away
figures.note: Advertising copy built from a flight time plus travel to and from airports. Treat as an invented example.

figures.claim: Faro Marina and Old Town are 0 km from Faro
figures.white_paper_wording: Faro Marina and Old Town (0 km from Faro)

primary.value: 2.6 km from Faro airport (straight line); in Faro itself
primary.publisher: Computed from OpenStreetMap coordinates (Marina de Faro 37.0151, -7.9363; Faro airport LPFR 37.0144, -7.9659)

figures.note: Great-circle (haversine). Coordinates are OpenStreetMap contributors' data, ODbL 1.0.

figures.claim: Vilamoura Marina is about 20 km west of Faro
figures.white_paper_wording: Vilamoura Marina (~20 km west of Faro)

primary.value: 15.4 km from Faro airport, 17.7 km from Marina de Faro (straight line), west
primary.publisher: Computed from OpenStreetMap coordinates (Marina de Vilamoura 37.0787, -8.1189)

figures.note: Within the paper's "about 20 km"; by road it is longer. Great-circle (haversine).

figures.claim: Praia da Falésia is about 30 km west of Faro
figures.white_paper_wording: Praia da Falésia (~30 km west of Faro)

primary.value: 17.9 km from Faro airport, 20.3 km from Marina de Faro (straight line, to the middle of the beach), west
primary.publisher: Computed from OpenStreetMap coordinates (Praia da Falésia 37.0805, -8.1495)

figures.note: About 18 to 20 km in a straight line, not 30. The beach is several kilometres long, between Vilamoura and Olhos de Água. Great-circle (haversine).

figures.claim: Albufeira Old Town and beach are about 30 km west of Faro
figures.white_paper_wording: Albufeira Old Town & Beach (~30 km west of Faro)

primary.value: 26.8 km from Faro airport, 29.2 km from Marina de Faro (straight line), west
primary.publisher: Computed from OpenStreetMap coordinates (Largo Engenheiro Duarte Pacheco, Albufeira, 37.0884, -8.2527)

figures.claim: Tavira riverfront is about 30 km east of Faro
figures.white_paper_wording: Tavira Riverfront (~30 km east of Faro)

primary.value: 30.7 km from Faro airport, 28.3 km from Marina de Faro (straight line), east
primary.publisher: Computed from OpenStreetMap coordinates (Ponte Romana, Tavira, 37.1269, -7.6498)

figures.claim: Sunset in the Algarve at 5:30pm when daylight in London ended at 4pm
figures.white_paper_wording: Sunset in Algarve at 5:30pm – daylight in London ended at 4pm

primary.value: Faro 17:21, London 16:08 on 18 November 2026; Faro 17:18, London 15:53 on 21 December; Faro 17:37, London 16:18 on 15 January (all UTC, which is local time in both in winter)
primary.publisher: Computed with NOAA's solar position equations (General Solar Position Calculations, NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory)

figures.note: About an hour and a quarter to an hour and a half more daylight in Faro in winter. Approximate to a minute or two; the screen can compute the day's times live and label them computed.

figures.claim: The UK is one of the Algarve's top tourist markets
figures.white_paper_wording: The UK is one of Algarve's top tourist markets
figures.note: News reports of INE data put the UK at about 34 to 36% of non-resident overnight stays in the Algarve in 2025, the largest foreign market, but INE's own table was not read in this round.

figures.claim: Searches and bookings for sunny destinations rise during bad weather at home
figures.white_paper_wording: travel sites report spikes in searches for sunny destinations during cold or rainy local weather
figures.note: The paper's source is a weather-advertising vendor's blog, not primary research.

figures.claim: A live 'midnight sun' billboard campaign in Vancouver inspired travel interest
figures.white_paper_wording: Similar campaigns (e.g. Tourism Yukon's live "midnight sun" billboards in Canada) have proven effective at inspiring travel
figures.note: The paper's source is a Pinterest pin. Do not repeat the effectiveness claim; if the precedent is mentioned at all, say it is reported, and do not suggest that tourism body has any link to this site.
